subChunks.title: Scroll Behaviour and Overflow Patterns
subChunks.hookHtml: Scroll behaviour is one of the most overlooked aspects of UI quality. Horizontal scroll on mobile, scrolling panels within a fixed layout, smooth anchor navigation, scroll snap for sliders — all require specific Tailwind utilities that most developers miss until something breaks.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Overflow utilities

overflow-auto      /* scroll only when needed (both axes) */
overflow-hidden    /* clip content — no scroll */
overflow-scroll    /* always show scrollbars */
overflow-visible   /* let content overflow (default) */

overflow-x-auto    /* horizontal scroll when needed */
overflow-y-auto    /* vertical scroll when needed */
overflow-x-hidden  /* hide horizontal overflow */
overflow-y-hidden  /* hide vertical overflow */

Scroll containers — internal scrolling

/* Panel that scrolls internally within a fixed-height parent */
<div class="h-screen flex flex-col">
  <header class="flex-none h-16 border-b">Header</header>
  <main class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-6">
    <!-- long scrollable content -->
  </main>
</div>

/* Horizontal scrolling tag list */
<div class="flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto pb-2 scrollbar-hide">
  <span class="flex-none px-3 py-1 bg-blue-100 rounded-full text-sm">Tag</span>
  <!-- many tags -->
</div>

Scroll snapping

/* Horizontal scroll carousel with snapping */
<div class="flex gap-4 overflow-x-auto
            snap-x snap-mandatory
            scroll-smooth">
  <div class="snap-start flex-none w-80">Card 1</div>
  <div class="snap-start flex-none w-80">Card 2</div>
  <div class="snap-start flex-none w-80">Card 3</div>
</div>

snap-x          /* snap on the x-axis */
snap-y          /* snap on the y-axis */
snap-mandatory  /* always snaps to a snap point */
snap-proximity  /* snaps if close enough */

snap-start      /* snap child to start */
snap-center     /* snap child to center */
snap-end        /* snap child to end */

Smooth scrolling

/* On the html element (or scroll container) */
scroll-smooth

/* Anchor padding — prevent content hiding under sticky header */
scroll-mt-20    /* 80px offset when scrolled to anchor */

<!-- The element with the anchor id -->
<section id="features" class="scroll-mt-20">

Scroll padding and margin

scroll-p-4      /* padding inside a scroll container */
scroll-pt-20    /* top padding — prevents sticky header overlap */
scroll-m-4      /* margin offset for anchored elements */
scroll-mt-16    /* margin-top — offset from sticky nav height */

overscroll behaviour

overscroll-contain   /* prevent scroll chaining — modal scrolls stay in modal */
overscroll-none      /* prevent pull-to-refresh and bounce effects */
overscroll-auto      /* default browser behaviour */

Hiding scrollbars (custom)

Tailwind v4 doesn't have a scrollbar-hide utility by default. Use the scrollbar Tailwind plugin or target with CSS:

/* In your CSS */
.no-scrollbar::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
.no-scrollbar { -ms-overflow-style: none; scrollbar-width: none; }

Master Ember: "overscroll-contain is the fix for the modal scroll problem — when a user scrolls to the bottom of a modal and continues scrolling, the page behind shouldn't move. Add overscroll-contain to the modal panel and scrolling stays contained."

storyBeats.speaker: Master Ember
storyBeats.text: The layout that works perfectly on desktop falls apart on mobile when a horizontal table causes full-page scroll. The modal that works visually breaks when users reach the bottom and scroll into the page behind it. These are not edge cases — they are daily bugs. overflow-x-auto and overscroll-contain are two of the most valuable utilities in the entire framework.

Build a horizontal scroll carousel and an internal-scroll panel:

  • .carousel: flex, gap-4, overflow-x-auto, snap-x, snap-mandatory, scroll-smooth, pb-2
  • .carousel-item: snap-start, flex-none, w-72, bg-white, rounded-xl, shadow-sm, p-5, border, border-gray-100
  • .scroll-panel: h-64, overflow-y-auto, overscroll-contain, border, border-gray-200, rounded-xl

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a complete scroll-aware layout from scratch: a sticky nav with scroll-mt-20 on all section anchors, a horizontal quest category carousel with snap scrolling, a fixed-height notifications panel with overscroll-contain and overflow-y-auto, and a responsive table wrapped in overflow-x-auto. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between overflow-auto and overflow-scroll. Walk through the snap-x snap-mandatory pattern for a carousel — what does each class contribute and what would a carousel without snap feel like? Explain overscroll-contain and the specific problem it solves for modals.

questions.prompt: A page has a sticky navigation bar 64px tall. When clicking anchor links, the target sections are partially hidden under the nav. Which class on the target sections fixes this?
options: scroll-mt-16 — adds a 64px scroll margin-top offset when the element is scrolled into view via an anchor link
pt-16 — adds padding-top to push content down
mt-16 — adds margin-top to offset the nav
top-16 — positions the element 64px from the top
questions.answer: scroll-mt-16 — adds a 64px scroll margin-top offset when the element is scrolled into view via an anchor link
questions.explanation: scroll-mt-{n} sets the scroll-margin-top CSS property, which adds an offset when an element is scrolled to via an anchor link or focus. When the user clicks an anchor (#section), the browser scrolls so the element appears 64px from the top — below the sticky nav. pt-16 would add visual padding, not a scroll offset, changing the layout of every section.

questions.prompt: A horizontal card carousel uses overflow-x-auto and the cards are flex-none. When swiped, cards scroll freely but don't stop at card boundaries — they stop at arbitrary positions. Which class on the container enables snapping to card positions?
options: snap-x snap-mandatory on the container, snap-start on each card
scroll-snap on the container, snap-point on each card
scroll-stop on the container — Tailwind handles the rest
questions.answer: snap-x snap-mandatory on the container, snap-start on each card
questions.explanation: snap-x enables horizontal scroll snapping on the container. snap-mandatory forces the scroll to always settle at a snap point (rather than stopping between items). Each card needs snap-start (or snap-center) to define its snap point. Without the snap-start on individual cards, the snap container has no defined snap points to lock onto.

questions.prompt: A modal has a long terms-of-service text. When the user scrolls to the bottom of the modal and keeps scrolling, the background page also scrolls. Which class on the modal panel prevents this scroll chaining?
options: overscroll-contain — contains scroll events within the element, preventing them from propagating to the parent
overflow-hidden — prevents any scrolling on the modal
position-fixed — fixes the modal in place preventing scroll
scroll-lock — Tailwind's built-in scroll lock utility
questions.answer: overscroll-contain — contains scroll events within the element, preventing them from propagating to the parent
questions.explanation: overscroll-contain sets overscroll-behavior: contain, which prevents scroll events from chaining to the parent once the element reaches its scroll boundary. Without it, reaching the bottom of the modal and continuing to scroll causes the background page to scroll (scroll chaining). This is the CSS-only solution to the modal scroll problem.
